title: Grateful Dead Live at East Hall, Franklin & Marshall College on 1971-04-10
lineage: SBD > MR > Cass > DAT > CD > EAC > CD Wave > shntool > mkwACT > SHN

ai_review.summary: A mostly crystal‑clear soundboard capture that leans guitar‑heavy, preserving a high‑energy 1971 show with standout performances of Good Lovin', Cumberland Blues and Loser.
ai_review.review: The April 10, 1971 Franklin & Marshall concert shines thanks to Jerry Garcia’s incendiary lead work, tight rhythm from Bob Weir and Phil Lesh’s “Phil bomb” bass lines, plus a set that keeps the crowd dancing from Good Lovin' through Sugar Magnolia. The soundboard source is generally clean and crisp, though the mix favors guitars over vocals and has a few brief drop‑outs (notably at the start of Truckin'). Overall the recording is very listenable and the performance is celebrated by fans as a classic early‑Seventies show.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently strong praise for musical energy and several standout songs (≈70% weight) combined with mostly good technical quality, offset by occasional mix‑balance complaints (≈30% weight).

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, crisp board recording but heavily guitar‑forward; vocals sit low in the mix, a few brief drop‑outs on Truckin' and occasional muddiness noted. Overall listenable with no major distortion.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
poor_songs: Bertha (noted as weak by one reviewer)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The first set builds momentum with strong jams on MABM and NTYSM, while the second set is described as “on fire” throughout, delivering sustained high energy.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for ‘playing his ass off’, guitar turned up to 11, heavy solo work, and even opening doors on stage; some reviewers note his mix dominates the sound.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for powerful bass “bombs”, driving jam intensity especially in the second set, and generally tight rhythm section contribution.
band_member_comments.Bob: Recognized for solid rhythm guitar riffs and strong interplay with Jerry; praised during China Cat and other jams.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey absent (1971), Billy’s drumming described as funky groove but often lower in the mix; overall drum feel described as solid.
